title: Websites for real estate brokerages | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs builds brokerage websites, agent directories, and web tools such as inquiry forms and onboarding portals. Fixed price, quoted after a call.
h1: Websites and web applications for real estate brokerages
intro: Many real estate brokerages have a website provided by their franchise or by a template vendor, with an IDX listing feed, an agent directory, and a contact form that routes to a general inbox. The pieces the office actually needs from the web tend to sit elsewhere: agent recruiting pages, a place for new agents to submit onboarding paperwork, and a way for sellers or referral partners to request a consultation. Those usually end up as PDFs emailed back and forth.

Creosote Labs builds the brokerage site and the tools behind it. A marketing site covers the office's services, agent profiles, and a clear way to book a consultation or a recruiting conversation. Behind it, we build the forms and portals staff use directly: an agent onboarding form that collects license numbers, W-9s, and independent contractor agreements, or a seller inquiry form that lands in the CRM as a lead. Hosting, domain setup, and written handover documentation are included.
projects: A brokerage marketing site with an agent directory, office information, and a booking link for buyer and seller consultations.
An agent recruiting page with a commission plan overview and an application form that goes straight to the broker.
An onboarding portal where a new agent uploads their license, W-9, and signed independent contractor agreement.
A home valuation request form that captures the property address and delivers the lead to Follow Up Boss or kvCORE.
A referral partner page where out-of-area agents submit a referral and receive confirmation.

faqs.q: Can the site keep the IDX listing search the office has now?
faqs.a: Yes. IDX feeds come from the MLS vendor and can be placed on a new site the same way they are on the current one. We confirm the vendor and feed during the scoping call.

faqs.q: Who owns the site after it is built?
faqs.a: The brokerage does. The domain, hosting account, and code are set up in the office's name, and handover includes written documentation for whoever maintains it.

faqs.q: What does a brokerage website cost?
faqs.a: Each project is quoted after a scoping call, and the quote is a fixed price for the agreed scope. There is no hourly billing.
